evidence: src/auth/auth.controller.ts: AuthController is constructor-injected with only AuthService, and every handler (register, login, refresh, profile, findAll, create, update, findOne, logOut, getRefreshToken, revokeToken) calls this.authService.*.

src/auth/auth.controller.ts: req.cookies['Refresh'] is hard-coded in both refresh() and logOut(), while cookie building lives in authService.getCookieForLogOut()/login(). This is a minor spread of cookie-name knowledge.
src/auth/auth.controller.ts logOut(): `const cookie = req.cookies['Refresh']` and `const refreshCookie = req.cookies['Refresh']` read the same value twice.

src/auth/auth.module.ts: LoginThrottleFactory builds the Redis client and RateLimiterRedis inline, and the 'process.env.X || config' fallbacks repeat in that factory and in the JwtModule.registerAsync factory.

src/auth/auth.module.ts: @Module registers controllers [AuthController], providers [AuthService, JwtTwoFactorStrategy, JwtStrategy, UniqueValidatorPipe, LoginThrottleFactory] and exports the auth abstractions, so the wiring covers a single feature.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The two files make up the presentation and wiring for one NestJS auth feature. auth.module.ts registers AuthController, AuthService, the JWT/Passport strategies and the login-throttle provider. auth.controller.ts sends every endpoint through the injected AuthService. Its concerns are registration and login, token refresh and logout, profile, user administration and session (refresh-token) listing. These are all identity and user-account concerns built around the same UserEntity and refresh-token aggregate. They are related, not separate concerns. The controller uses the module's own abstractions throughout: it calls AuthService for business logic, GetUser for the current user, and JwtTwoFactorGuard/PermissionGuard for access control. It never reaches into UserRepository or the Redis client directly. There are some small cohesion weaknesses, but none rises to a rubric failure. First, the cookie name 'Refresh' is hard-coded in both AuthController.refresh and AuthController.logOut, while the service owns cookie building (getCookieForLogOut), so knowledge of the cookie name is spread across two layers. Second, logOut reads req.cookies['Refresh'] twice into two separate variables. Third, auth.module.ts builds the Redis client and repeats the 'process.env.X || config.y' fallback pattern inside LoginThrottleFactory and the JwtModule factory. That is infrastructure wiring, but it is common in Nest modules and stays within one file. Mixing admin user CRUD (/users) into AuthController is debatable, but it covers the same User aggregate and service.
